parts.text: A student tests two solids: solid F and solid G. Tests on solid F Solid F is calcium carbonate.

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text:
M1 limewater becomes milky
M2 effervescence / fizzing / bubbling

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student filters the product from (a) to obtain solution H as the filtrate. The student divides solution H into three approximately equal portions in three test-tubes.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) To the second portion of solution H, the student adds aqueous sodium hydroxide dropwise and then in excess. observations when added dropwise .................................................................................. observations in excess ...................................................................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(b)(ii)
ms.text:
dropwise: white precipitate
excess: no (further) change / precipitate remains / white precipitate / insoluble

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) To the third portion of solution H, the student adds about 1 cm depth of dilute nitric acid followed by a few drops of aqueous silver nitrate. observations ...................................................................................................................... ..................................................................................................................................... [1] Tests on solid G Table 3.1 shows the tests and the student’s observations for solid G. Table 3.1 tests observations test 1 Do a flame test on solid G. lilac coloured flame test 2 Dissolve the remaining solid G in water to form solution G. Divide solution G into three portions. To the first portion of solution G, add about 1 cm 3 of aqueous chlorine. orange solution forms test 3 To the second portion of solution G, add about 1 cm 3 of aqueous sodium hydroxide. remains colourless test 4 To the third portion of solution G, add about 1 cm 3 of dilute nitric acid followed by a few drops of aqueous silver nitrate. cream precipitate forms
